agent_messages.content: [scientist_B → scientist_A] Critique: I am not convinced yet: (1) 'Hot 32 °C 5 h -> cool 18 °C' is predicted to reach 1.53× peak rise (overproof risk 68%) — the same failure mode that plausibly made the warm loaf dense; end at the plateau rather than the clock. (3) only two judged loaves calibrate the sourness scale and the fitted slope is steep (×4.9), so small model errors become large predicted sourness differences. (4) timing sensitivity: at 32 °C each extra hour adds ≈0.22× of peak-rise progress (heuristic), so the step-down must happen on time. Decision for chamber B: 'Steady 27 °C, 10 h (capped)'. result.safety_note: Recommended schedules are proposals selected only from a validated candidate library (4-35 °C, no hold at or above 27 °C longer than 10 h, ramps ≤ 20 °C/h). The local API clamps every setpoint and the ESP32 firmware independently enforces temperature limits, sensor-failure handling, fan protection and safe heating/cooling switching. Neither the LLM nor judge text can set power or bypass these checks, and ending fermentation/baking requires human confirmation.
